alerts.alert: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.desc: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS).
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

alerts.name: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
alerts.desc: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.
alerts.solution: Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers.

alerts.name: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
alerts.desc: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff'.

alerts.name: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
alerts.desc: A cookie has been set without the HttpOnly flag, which means that the cookie can be accessed by JavaScript.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set for all cookies.

alerts.name: Cookie without SameSite Attribute
alerts.desc: A cookie has been set without the SameSite attribute, which means that the cookie can be sent as a result of a 'cross-site' request.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.

alerts.alert: Server Leaks Version Information via "Server" HTTP Response Header Field
alerts.name: Server Leaks Version Information via "Server" HTTP Response Header Field
alerts.desc: The web/application server is leaking version information via the "Server" HTTP response header.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to suppress the "Server" header.

alerts.name: Permissions Policy Header Not Set
alerts.desc: Permissions Policy Header is an added layer of security that helps to restrict from unauthorized access or usage of browser/client features by web resources.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Permissions-Policy header.
